title: Extension of maps from a nodal trait curve without rational target curves
statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $F$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $C\to T$ be H-projective, flat and finitely presented, with nonempty connected reduced geometric fibres of pure dimension one and smooth geometrically integral generic fibre $C_F$. Suppose that at every singular point of a geometric fibre its completed local ring is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$, where $\Omega$ is the algebraically closed geometric residue field. Let $X\to T$ be H-projective, and suppose every $\Omega$-morphism $\mathbf P^1_\Omega\to X_\Omega$ is constant for every geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$; constant means that it factors through an $\Omega$-point of $X_\Omega$. For every $F$-morphism $u:C_F\to X_F$, let $\Gamma$ be the reduced closure of its graph in $C\times_TX$. Then $C$ and $\Gamma$ are integral, $C$ is normal, and the graph projection $p:\Gamma\to C$ is an isomorphism. In particular $u$ extends to a $T$-morphism $C\to X$. The target $X$ is not assumed flat or integral, and $u$ may be constant.

Discrete valuation rings, affine spectra, H-projectivity, flatness and finite presentation are [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-flat-morphism] and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Smoothness, geometric integrality, geometric fibres, dimension, completion, power series, the projective line, fibre products, integrality and reduction are [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], [def-sc-p1-standard], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-pc-integral-scheme] and [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. Reduced graph closure is the closure of the graph with reduced induced closed subscheme structure [def-weil-closed-immersion].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-generic-nodal-trait-normality] to $C/T$. All its hypotheses are among ours; $C_F$ is integral. Hence $C$ is integral and normal and $C_F$ is dense. A DVR is Noetherian since every ideal is principal. By [lem-pc-projective-proper], $C\to T$ and $X\to T$ are proper, hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $C$ Noetherian. In particular $X\to T$ is separated.

source.place: Lemma 3.13, printed p.609, graph domination and contraction; agent-formulated no-rational-maps variant. Publisher PDF read online; archival PDF WANTED.

proof.text: The graph of $u$ is closed in $(C\times_TX)_F$: its graph immersion is the base change of the closed diagonal of $X/T$ along $(c,x)\mapsto(u(c),x)$, so use [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. The graph is isomorphic to the integral $C_F$. Its closure is irreducible (two closed subsets covering the closure would cover its dense irreducible subset). Give this closure the reduced induced structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. It is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. On the open generic fibre it equals the original graph: topological closure commutes with restriction to an open, and the two reduced closed structures agree by the cited uniqueness. Therefore $p_F:\Gamma_F\to C_F$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-projective-base-change], $C\times_TX\to C$ is H-projective. Choose its closed embedding into $\mathbf P^N_C$ using [def-kun-projective]. Compose this embedding with the closed immersion $\Gamma\hookrightarrow C\times_TX$ using [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp]; this exhibits $p$ as H-projective. It is proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper]. Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-trait-rational-domination] to this integral $\Gamma$ and $p$, using $p_F$ from Step 2. Obtain $h:Y\to C$ and a proper surjective $C$-map $a:Y\to\Gamma$, with $pa=h$, whose reduced geometric fibres are points or connected finite unions of projective lines.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $c:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to C$ and its composite $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$. The reduction of $Y_c$ has the same underlying points as $Y_c$ by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. If it is a point, its image in $X_\Omega$ is a singleton. Otherwise each of its finitely many components is $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$ by Step 3. Its map to $X_\Omega$ is constant by our hypothesis. Components that meet have the same image point, by evaluating at a point of their intersection. Their incidence graph is connected: a partition without an edge would partition the finite closed cover into two disjoint nonempty closed-and-open subsets. Thus all components have the same image point. The embedding $\Gamma_c\hookrightarrow X_\Omega$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Moreover $a_c:Y_c\to\Gamma_c$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Consequently $|\Gamma_c|$ is a singleton. This is a claim about underlying points only; no reducedness of $\Gamma_c$ or scheme-theoretic contraction is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 3.13, printed p.609, graph domination and contraction; agent-formulated no-rational-maps variant. Publisher PDF read online; archival PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Every ordinary fibre $\Gamma_d$ has at most one point, since its projection from the geometric fibre over an algebraic closure of $\kappa(d)$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], applied to the surjective field-extension map. Thus $p$ is proper with finite fibres. Since $C$ is locally Noetherian by Step 1, [thm-pqf-finite-iff-proper-finite-fibres] makes $p$ finite. The isomorphism $p_F$ between nonempty dense integral opens identifies the function fields of $\Gamma$ and $C$. The target $C$ is normal, so [lem-trf-finite-birational-normal-iso] makes $p$ an isomorphism. Compose its inverse with $\Gamma\to X$ to obtain the required $T$-morphism; on $C_F$ it is $u$ by construction of the graph. No step used flatness or integrality of $X$, or nonconstancy of $u$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q41-3d39f13d0 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full, all 5 steps and every cited statement. There are no new nodes and the statement is unchanged; I found no repair note, so this is an ordinary one-level split. Checks: Step 1 meets every hypothesis of the normality node, so C is integral, normal and Noetherian (a DVR is Noetherian). In Step 2 the graph is the pullback of the closed diagonal (I checked the equalizer); the reduced closure is integral, and uniqueness in reduced-induced (3) gives Γ_F = graph. In Step 3 the closed immersions Γ↪C×X↪P^N_C compose, so p is H-projective. The rational-domination node (reviewed pass, Q48) has the same hypotheses on C and gives Y→Γ proper surjective with fibres that are a point or a connected finite union of P^1_Ω. Step 4 is correct topology: each P^1 component is constant, so connectedness gives one image point; Γ_c↪X_Ω and a_c surjective then give |Γ_c|≤1. In Step 5 the fibres are finite (a geometric fibre surjects onto the ordinary fibre), 02OG (C locally Noetherian) makes p finite, and 0AB1 makes it an isomorphism because the function fields agree and C is normal. Small cases tested: u constant, nonreduced or nonflat X, xy=π^n, and the X=P^1 counterexample, which the hypothesis correctly excludes. Minor point, not a fault: lem-pc-projective-proper and lem-pc-projective-base-change are stated for projective = H-projective + quasi-compact, and an H-projective morphism is quasi-compact in one line; rational-domination already uses the same convention. No duplicate among the extension/contraction nodes I searched. The declared tool_uses are generic and accepted. Batch-5: the trf nodes in rational-domination's closure (H-projective composition, projective bundles, Stein connectedness) and lem-trf-finite-birational-normal-iso (Stacks 0AB1) are generic scheme theory and commutative algebra, outside the trace-formula and Poincaré-duality assumptions, so both are accepted. No SGA source is cited; de Jong 3.13 stays WANTED with proof_origin agent.
